entries.topic: Peter Thiel's own texts: Cato 2009, Straussian Moment 2004/2007, Zero to One 2014, privacy op-ed 2016, statements on democracy

claims.text: Cato 2009: 'Most importantly, I no longer believe that freedom and democracy are compatible.'; 'The 1920s were the last decade in American history during which one could be genuinely optimistic about politics.'; 'find an escape from politics in all its forms'; 'The fate of our world may depend on the effort of a single person who builds or propagates the machinery of freedom'; Thiel was 'a Stanford undergraduate studying philosophy in the late 1980s'

Follow-up (Editor's Note): 'It would be absurd to suggest that women's votes will be taken away or that this would solve the political problems that vex us.'; 'While I don't think any class of people should be disenfranchised, I have little hope that voting will make things better.'; 'Voting is not under siege in America, but many other rights are.'; people 'imprisoned for using even very mild drugs, tortured by our own government, and forced to bail out reckless financial companies'; 'Politics is about interfering with other people's lives without their consent.'; 'I advocate focusing energy elsewhere, onto peaceful projects that some consider utopian.'

'The Straussian Moment' was published in Politics and Apocalypse, ed. Robert Hamerton-Kelly, Michigan State UP 2007, pp. 189-218; it opens with 11 September 2001; proposes considering Echelon, the secret coordination of intelligence services, rather than a United Nations of endless parliamentary debates, as a decisive path to a Pax Americana; says the Straussian project aims to preserve the katechon; treats Schmitt's politics as the field where humans must choose friends and enemies; discusses Locke replacing human nature with an unknown X; discusses Girard's mimetic rivalry and scapegoat and contrasts Girard with Strauss; ends advising the Christian statesman to side with peace

Thiel first delivered the lecture at his self-funded 2004 conference 'Politics and the Apocalypse'; English phrases quoted by LARB: 'the new science of economics and the practice of capitalism filled the vacuum'; Thiel quoting Strauss 'The most just society cannot survive without "intelligence," i.e., espionage'; Harper says Vance's term 'Christian statesman' comes from the essay (her reading)
Thiel's WSJ essay 'Competition Is for Losers' (Review section, September 2014) was adapted from Zero to One

Zero to One: 'Competition is for losers'; justifies 'creative monopolies' as distinct from 'illegal bullies or government favourites'; 'ideology of competition'; 'Monopolists lie to protect themselves'; Google framed itself 'as just another tech company'; in a debate with Eric Schmidt Thiel said a monopoly like Google's in search is 'quite legal' if not abused

Thiel op-ed 15 Aug 2016: 'A free press is vital for public debate'; 'It is ridiculous to claim that journalism requires indiscriminate access to private people's sex lives'; 'Protecting individual dignity online is a long-term project'; said he 'would gladly support someone else in the same position'; Gawker outed Thiel in 2007
Gellman (Atlantic, Nov 2023): Thiel wanted published a promise that he 'wouldn't be giving money to any politician, including Donald Trump, in the next presidential campaign' (Gellman's paraphrase)

Carl Schmitt (1888-1985), German jurist and political theorist, joined the Nazi Party in 1933, helped legally coordinate the Nazi seizure of power and endorsed Hitler's murder of political adversaries and anti-Jewish policies

entries.topic: Girard, Imitatio, the Douthat interview, the Antichrist lectures and the katechon

claims.text: Imitatio was co-founded in 2007 by Thiel and Robert Hamerton-Kelly and is one of three Thiel Foundation ventures; Girard, a Stanford professor of French and Italian, influenced Thiel through mimetic theory

Thiel: 'I met him when I was a student at Stanford in the late 1980s'; on Things Hidden: 'It felt like you understood the meaning of history'; Vance: Thiel's Yale talk 'remains the most significant moment of my time at Yale Law School'; article dates Imitatio to 2008

Douthat interview 26 June 2025: Douthat 'This is a long hesitation.'; 'Should the human race survive?' Thiel: 'Yes.'; 'The slogan of the Antichrist is "peace and safety"'; 'one world totalitarian state'; 'In our world, it's far more likely to be Greta Thunberg.'; populism 'still by far the best option we have'; 2024 'the year where Elon stopped believing in Mars'; to Douthat's point that he is 'deeply invested in Palantir, in military technology' and surveillance: 'I obviously don't think that that's what I'm doing.'

National Review version of the exchange: Douthat 'I think you would prefer the human race to endure, right?' Thiel: 'Well, I don't know. I would — I would ——' Douthat: 'Should the human race survive?' Thiel: 'Yes.'

Four-part Antichrist lectures at the Commonwealth Club, San Francisco, organised by the nonprofit Acts 17 Collective, Sept–Oct 2025; drawing on Girard, Francis Bacon and Carl Schmitt; sold out, off the record

First lecture Monday 15 September 2025; Bay Resistance protest outside citing Palantir and ICE; attendees: Antichrist as a scenario, a one-world government suppressing technology or AI ending the world

Washington Post reviewed audio of all four lectures; forensic expert Hany Farid found a sample probably authentic; Thiel called critics of technology including Greta Thunberg 'legionnaires of the Antichrist'; Post paraphrase: those proposing limits on technology threaten destruction of the US and global totalitarian rule

Reason on the leaked lectures: Thiel called the American empire 'the natural candidate for Katechon' and also 'ground zero of the one-world state'; warned of a 'caesaropapist one-world state'; named tax treaties, financial surveillance and sanctions architecture; 'in the 21st century, the Antichrist is a Luddite who wants to stop all science'; listed Yudkowsky, Bostrom and Thunberg; called himself 'a humble classical liberal'

Paris, 26 January 2026, Académie des sciences morales et politiques, working group on the future of democracy, introduced by Chantal Delsol: 'je m'inquiète de l'Antéchrist'; 'l'Antéchrist est un luddite qui veut mettre fin à toute science'; protest outside
Cambridge: closed 'Antichrist Lectures' at St Catharine's College, late January/early February 2026, hosted by divinity academic James Orr, a Reform UK adviser; invitation only

Rome: closed-door, invitation-only lectures from Sunday 15 March 2026 to the Wednesday; Catholic universities denied hosting; papal AI adviser Paolo Benanti called Thiel a 'political theologian'; no meeting with Pope Leo on the agenda

Katechon: 'that which withholds' / 'the one who withholds', 2 Thessalonians 2:6-7; tradition links it to the Roman Empire and emperor; other proposals the Church, the Holy Spirit; Schmitt in Nomos of the Earth treated the katechon as central to Rome-centred Christianity, restraining the Antichrist
Thiel sees the katechon as a restraining force that holds back the spirit of the Antichrist; Paul never explains what the restraining force is

entries.topic: Practice against philosophy: Palantir, government revenue, electoral spending

claims.text: Thiel (Fortune 2016): 'The government was collecting a lot of data ... more than they could analyze ... If we could help them make sense of data, they could end indiscriminate surveillance.'

Palantir sued the Army in 2016 in the Court of Federal Claims under the Federal Acquisition Streamlining Act of 1994 for shutting out commercial products from DCGS-A; won in October 2016; in March 2019 won a DCGS-A contract worth up to $876 million over 10 years
Palantir FY2025 revenue $4.475 billion; US government revenue $1.855 billion, up 55%

Per FEC records cited by CNBC: Thiel gave $15 million to a pro-Vance super PAC and $15 million plus $2.5 million in October to a pro-Masters super PAC in 2022; overall midterm investment $32 million; Vance won, Masters lost
Thiel and Naval Ravikant together invested more than $200,000 in Clearview AI; the investments later converted into equity (individual share not given)
